messages:
maria_sec: Heads up — compliance just failed the weekly report. Found ~12 role.update events missing target_resource_id and the actor is 'kms-service@redwood'. Not sure if this is audit producer bug or header loss. Anyone?

devon_infra: I flipped the rbac-proxy refactor flag last week (drop_missing_headers=true) during cleanup. Did we think that would be safe?

kevin_audit: I pulled the rows: count = 12 for event='role.update' and target_resource_id IS NULL for 2026-03-18..2026-03-19. Exported sample to /tmp/missing_audit_2171234567.csv

maria_sec: @kevin_audit can you paste a single sanitized row so we can see fields?

kevin_audit: ```json
{"event":"role.update","actor":"kms-service@redwood","actor_type":"service","actor_claims":"service_account:rbac-proxy","target":"","changes":[{"role":"admin","granted":false}],"metadata":{"kms_key":"projects/redwood/locations/global/keyR1"}}
```

olivia_prodeng: That target empty string is suspicious. rbac-proxy should forward X-Resource-ID to audit. We did change header behavior when hardening the proxy.

devon_infra: yeah that was my change — I set drop_missing_headers=true to enforce strictness across internal services. I didn't realize audit depended on an existing header and would write blank instead of failing loudly. My bad. Rolling back now.

sam_sre: Before rollback: do we have enough info to backfill those 12 events? Any correlation ids in request logs?

kevin_audit: 10/12 have X-Req-Id in auth-proxy logs. 2 are from async rbac-worker runs (no req-id). I can correlate by (actor_claims, timestamp, role_change_details) to rbac-store for those. Backfill seems doable for 10 and best-effort for 2.

maria_sec: Another angle: audit entries show actor="kms-service" which obscures the human initiator. For compliance we need initiator or actor_chain so the chain of callers is preserved (user -> rbac-proxy -> kms). Recommend adding actor_chain array to audit schema.

devon_infra: agree. I'll open a PR to: 1) restore header forwarding, 2) add actor_chain enrichment in rbac-proxy before sending to audit. Rolling back drop_missing_headers now.

ci-bot: Deploy triggered: rbac-proxy/config rollback -> staging. Build #4532.

olivia_prodeng: After the rollback, re-run the compliance query and sanity-check counts. @kevin_audit can you re-run once deployed?

kevin_audit: Will re-run in ~30m after staging verifies. Preliminary check: events after 2171234580 have target_resource_id present.

maria_sec: I'll open a Jira for the backfill + schema change (need audit trail for SOC). CER-214. Also drafting a playbook for backfilling async events.

devon_infra: PR merged: https://git.redwood.com/r/rbac-proxy/merge/1234 — header restore + actor_chain stub.

kevin_audit: Re-run query: missing count drops to 0 post-rollback. Backfill plan: map rows by (actor_claims, timestamp, change payload) and populate target_resource_id where deterministic; flag 2 uncertain events for manual review.

sam_sre: Sounds good. Let us know when backfill is in prod. I'll shadow run the compliance report and compare diffs.

maria_sec: Thanks everyone. Leaving notes in CER-214 and will post completion when backfill done. Closing loop here. :white_check_mark:
